## Solution Provider Compliance Requirements

Taxpayers may choose any e-invoicing solution provider as long as it is compliant with the e-invoicing requirements, and ZATCA will consider the taxpayer's compliance if they are complying with the e-invoicing requirements even if the solution provider is not listed on the indicative list.

The indicative list of solution providers on ZATCA's website who have passed the qualification process and criteria aims to allow taxpayers to easily reach potential solution providers.

## Important Note on Certification

It's important to understand that ZATCA certifies the specific e-invoicing solution of a specific business entity, not ERP product lines. What ZATCA evaluates and certifies is the specific e-invoicing solution—the exact configuration of a specific business entity. The certification binds a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to a specific device and solution configuration, not to an ERP product line.

## Technical Requirements for Third-Party Providers

ZATCA's technical specification for Phase 2 mandates six specific capabilities. Any e-invoicing solution — whether embedded in an ERP or standalone — must implement all six to pass the Compliance CSID process.

Based on the search results, here's what I found about ZATCA e-invoicing solution provider accreditation requirements for third-party software:

## Solution Provider Compliance Requirements

Taxpayers may choose any e-invoicing solution provider as long as it is compliant with the e-invoicing requirements, and ZATCA will consider the taxpayer's compliance if they are complying with the e-invoicing requirements even if the solution provider is not listed on the indicative list.

The indicative list of solution providers on ZATCA's website who have passed the qualification process and criteria aims to allow taxpayers to easily reach potential solution providers.

## Important Note on Certification

It's important to understand that ZATCA certifies the specific e-invoicing solution of a specific business entity, not ERP product lines. What ZATCA evaluates and certifies is the specific e-invoicing solution—the exact configuration of a specific business entity. The certification binds a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN) to a specific device and solution configuration, not to an ERP product line.

## Technical Requirements for Third-Party Providers

ZATCA's technical specification for Phase 2 mandates six specific capabilities. Any e-invoicing solution — whether embedded in an ERP or standalone — must implement all six to pass the Compliance CSID process.
